title: Second moment of the centered linear square
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $a_1,\ldots,a_n\in\mathbb{R}$. For a uniformly chosen $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, set $L(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i$. Then one half of the average of $\left(L(x)^2-\sum_{i=1}^n a_i^2\right)^2$ equals $\left(\sum_{i=1}^n a_i^2\right)^2-\sum_{i=1}^n a_i^4$.
hypotheses_covered: $a$ assigns a real coefficient to each coordinate
